items.review_rationale: Read a Z-graded module over a nonnegatively graded ring, with a direct sum decomposition and compatible degree addition under S_n multiplication, distinguishing grading of scalars and modules.

references.context: Every module element is uniquely a finite sum of homogeneous components drawn from the degree-indexed additive subgroups.
Degree-j additive subgroup of M, compatible with the S-action.
Products of scalar degree-n and module degree-j elements lie in module degree n+j.

references.phrase: ring indices nonnegative; module indices integer
references.disposition: The base graded ring may have only n≥0, while the graded module may have negative degrees.

items.review_rationale: Read graded module degree shift M(n) using the exact component convention M(n)_j=M_{n+j}, preserving underlying S-module structure and avoiding the opposite shift convention.

references.context: Regrading of the same underlying module: degree j in M(n) is degree n+j in M.

references.disposition: Only the degree assignment is altered; ring action and ungraded module elements are preserved.

items.review_rationale: Read the direct-sum decomposition of a ring indexed by nonnegative integers, degree pieces as additive groups and multiplicative compatibility S_n S_m⊆S_{n+m}.

references.context: Every element has a unique finite homogeneous decomposition among additively indexed components.
Products of homogeneous components of degrees n,m have degree n+m.

references.disposition: This formulation imposes S_n only for n≥0; it does not require negative-degree pieces.
